questions.q: Why was Ridge regression chosen as the production model over Random Forest?
options: Ridge's out-of-sample IC was significant while Random Forest's was not, because Random Forest overfits with only 11 cross-sectional names
Random Forest cannot be exposed through pybind11
Ridge requires no validation at all
Ridge trains faster on a laptop
questions.explain: Ridge's OOS mean IC (~0.045, t≈2.1) is significant, while Random Forest's (~0.018, t≈0.9) is not — Random Forest overfits given only 11 names in the cross-section.

questions.q: What does the naive rank-reversal baseline do?
options: Uses Random Forest with default hyperparameters
Ranks sectors by trailing 5-day return and bets on reversal, with no machine learning involved
Trains on the full 2007–2025 sample with no validation split
Fits a Ridge regression with no regularization
questions.explain: The naive baseline is not ML at all — it simply ranks sectors by their trailing 5-day return and bets on mean reversion, serving as the bar every model must clear.

questions.q: Why does purged walk-forward cross-validation include a 5-day embargo?
options: To match the VIX term-structure slope
Because overlapping forward-5-day labels near a train/test boundary could otherwise leak information across it
To speed up training in the C++ core
Because scikit-learn requires it for Ridge models
questions.explain: The forward 5-day target creates overlapping labels near each train/test boundary; the embargo purges those overlapping labels so no information leaks across the split.

questions.q: What does the Information Coefficient (IC) measure?
options: The annualized volatility of the signal
The Spearman rank correlation between a model's predicted forward rank and the realized forward rank
The dollar P&L of the strategy
The number of sectors in the current universe
questions.explain: IC is the Spearman correlation between predicted and realized forward-5-day rank, averaged across out-of-sample periods with a t-stat to judge significance.

questions.q: Roughly how many out-of-sample evaluation periods does the purged walk-forward validation produce across 2012–2025?
options: Exactly 11, one per sector
About 18
About 180 weekly periods
About 1,800 daily periods
questions.explain: The expanding-window walk-forward scheme, evaluated weekly from 2012 through 2025, produces roughly 180 out-of-sample periods.
